boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain Binghamton University
boards.description: Explore the essential late-night rituals at Binghamton University, from on-campus Nite Owl grill sessions to the legendary diners and pizzerias that fuel late-hour study breaks.

cards.title: Appalachian Nite Owl
cards.subtitle: Mountainview Community
cards.notes: Hike up to Mountainview for late-night grill favorites like chicken nuggets and ice cream, served until 1 a.m. most nights.
cards.short_summary: A hilltop dining destination offering late-night grill options for the Mountainview and Hinman communities.
cards.evidence_claim: Appalachian Nite Owl is open all week from 9 p.m. to 1 a.m., serving items like chicken nuggets and ice cream.
cards.source_title: Hungry? A spotlight on campus dining halls.
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM daily during the academic semester.

cards.title: C4 Nite Owl
cards.subtitle: Newing and Dickinson Communities
cards.notes: Visit the ground floor of C4 for late-night burgers and snacks, a central hub for students in Newing and Dickinson.
cards.short_summary: The primary late-night dining hub for the Newing and Dickinson residential communities, open until 1 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: C4 Nite Owl is open from 9:00 PM to 1:00 AM for late-night dining hall access with grill options.
cards.source_title: Binghamton University Dining Transition Updates
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM during the academic semester.

cards.title: Binghamton Hots
cards.subtitle: Downtown Binghamton
cards.notes: Head downtown for the signature 'Hot Plate' or a late-night burger at this student favorite, open until 3:30 a.m. on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A downtown staple famous for its late-night plates and burgers, catering specifically to the student crowd.
cards.evidence_claim: Binghamton Hots is open until 3:30 a.m. on weekends and serves burgers, sandwiches, and vegetarian options.
cards.source_title: Cheap, greasy, delicious: The best late night food spots
cards.access_notes: Open until 3:30 AM on Fridays and Saturdays.

cards.title: Pasquale's Pizza
cards.subtitle: State Street
cards.notes: Grab a slice at this State Street landmark, known for serving the late-night crowd until 4:30 a.m. on weekends.
cards.short_summary: A popular downtown pizzeria that stays open into the early morning hours to serve students.
cards.evidence_claim: Pasquale's is open until 4:30 a.m. on weekends and is a popular spot for students after downtown activities.
cards.source_title: Cheap, greasy, delicious: The best late night food spots
cards.access_notes: Open until 4:30 AM on weekends.

cards.title: The Undergrounds Lounge
cards.subtitle: University Union
cards.notes: Study or relax in the basement of the Union, which stays open until 1 a.m. on weekends for bowling, pool, and late-night events.
cards.short_summary: A versatile student space in the University Union featuring games, study areas, and late-night programming.
cards.evidence_claim: The Undergrounds Lounge is open until midnight Sunday-Thursday and until 1 a.m. on Fridays and Saturdays.
cards.source_title: 11 of the Best Study Spaces in Binghamton
cards.access_notes: Open until 1:00 AM on Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.title: Bartle Library 24/7
cards.subtitle: Main Campus
cards.notes: During finals week, this central library becomes a 24-hour sanctuary for students powering through end-of-semester exams.
cards.short_summary: The university's main library, which extends its hours to 24/7 during the final exam period.
cards.evidence_claim: Bartle Library is open for studying 24/7 during finals week.
cards.source_title: #StudyBing | Student Transition and Success
cards.access_notes: 24-hour access available specifically during final exam periods.

cards.title: Late Nite Binghamton
cards.subtitle: University Union
cards.notes: Join weekend events like escape rooms and movies at the Union, providing safe, late-night entertainment for all students.
cards.short_summary: A university-sponsored program offering large-scale social events on Friday and Saturday nights.
cards.evidence_claim: Late Nite Binghamton hosts events like escape rooms and movies in the University Union on Friday and Saturday nights.
cards.source_title: Late Nite | Campus Activities
cards.access_notes: Events typically held on Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.title: The Spot Diner
cards.subtitle: Upper Front Street
cards.notes: A classic diner run for cheese fries or breakfast at any hour, serving the Binghamton community for decades.
cards.short_summary: A traditional 24-hour diner known for its extensive menu and popularity with students late at night.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spot Restaurant on Upper Front Street serves standard diner food and is a well-known late-night spot for students.
cards.source_title: Cheap, greasy, delicious: The best late night food spots
cards.access_notes: Traditionally open 24 hours; verify current seasonal hours locally.

cards.title: Hinman C-Store
cards.subtitle: Hinman Dining Center
cards.notes: Grab snacks, drinks, or quick meals until 10 p.m. at this convenient shop located within the Hinman community.
cards.short_summary: A campus convenience store providing late-evening food and supply options for Hinman residents.
cards.evidence_claim: The Hinman C-Store is open until 10:00 PM daily during the academic semester.
cards.source_title: Binghamton University Dining Transition Updates
cards.access_notes: Open until 10:00 PM daily.

cards.title: Bearcat Express UDC
cards.subtitle: University Downtown Center
cards.notes: Access 24-hour self-service snacks and Starbucks coffee at the downtown campus, perfect for late-night study sessions.
cards.short_summary: A 24-hour automated market providing food and beverages to students at the University Downtown Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Downtown Center features Bearcat Express, a convenient 24-hour self-service market.
cards.source_title: Binghamton University Dining Transition Updates
cards.access_notes: 24-hour self-service availability.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other

cards.title: The Remodeled Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Glenn G. Bartle Library

cards.evidence_claim: The newly remodeled third floor features a variety of seating options perfect for group or individual study.

cards.title: The Innovation Lab
cards.subtitle: University Union

cards.title: Science 2 Window Tables

cards.title: John Arthur Café
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Building

cards.evidence_claim: John Arthur Café has floor-to-ceiling windows and is located on the same floor as the Fine Arts lounge.

cards.title: The Undergrounds Lounge
cards.subtitle: University Union Basement
cards.notes: Choose this spot for group work if you prefer background noise; it's located near the bowling alley and Food Co-Op.
cards.short_summary: A lower-level lounge in the University Union that balances social activity with group study space.
cards.evidence_claim: The University Undergrounds Lounge is located in the basement of the University Union and is a great place for group projects.

cards.access_notes: Open late, until 1am on Fridays and Saturdays during the academic year.

cards.title: The Wooden Footbridge
cards.subtitle: Binghamton University Nature Preserve
cards.notes: Walk the 11 miles of trails to find this bridge over the wetlands, a popular spot for observing local wildlife like beavers.
cards.short_summary: A key landmark within the 190-acre campus nature preserve used for recreation and field study.
cards.evidence_claim: The preserve includes a number of maintained hiking trails and a wooden footbridge.
cards.source_title: About Nature Preserve - Binghamton University

cards.title: The South Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: Bartle Library 2nd Floor
cards.notes: Access the outdoor patio from this second-floor lounge, which provides a mix of individual and group seating.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor library lounge featuring an outdoor patio and various seating configurations.
cards.evidence_claim: South Study Lounge: 2nd floor lounge with outdoor patio, individual and group seating.
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms and Study Spaces | Libraries - Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Open during Bartle Library operating hours; patio access is weather-dependent.

cards.title: Engineering Lecture Hall Lounge
cards.subtitle: Engineering Building
cards.notes: Find this large lounge area located just outside the main lecture hall for a quiet alternative to the libraries.
cards.short_summary: A spacious student lounge area in the Engineering Building often used for quiet study between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: The Engineering Building has a large lounge area outside of its lecture hall that serves as a great spot.
cards.source_title: Bye bye Bartle: The best spots to study on campus - Pipe Dream
cards.access_notes: Open during standard academic building hours.

cards.title: Hinman Rooftop Seating
cards.subtitle: Hinman Dining Hall
cards.notes: Take your meal or books to the third-floor outdoor rooftop for a unique open-air perspective of the Hinman community.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor seating area located on the roof of the Hinman Dining Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Hinman Dining Hall is a spacious, three-story building with outdoor rooftop seating.
cards.source_title: Dining Hauls: A Tour of Binghamton's Delicious Dining Options
cards.access_notes: Accessible during dining hall hours; check seasonal availability for outdoor seating.

cards.title: Science Library Study Rooms
cards.subtitle: Science Library
cards.notes: Reserve one of the three group rooms on the first floor for a quieter, more focused environment than the main library.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group study rooms located on the first floor of the Science Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Group Study Rooms (reservable): Three rooms on the 1st floor of the Science Library.

cards.access_notes: Rooms must be reserved in advance via the library's online booking system.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Discover the best social and recreational spots at Binghamton University that require no admission fees or purchases. From nature trails to late-night bowling, these student-friendly activities are completely free with a university ID.

cards.title: Hike the Nature Preserve
cards.subtitle: 190 acres of trails and wetlands
cards.notes: Explore 11 miles of maintained trails and a wooden footbridge over Harpur Pond. It is open daily from dawn to dusk for hiking and wildlife spotting.
cards.short_summary: A sprawling 190-acre natural area on campus featuring diverse ecosystems and extensive hiking trails.
cards.evidence_claim: The Nature Preserve includes a number of maintained hiking trails and a wooden footbridge and is free for the university community.
cards.source_title: Binghamton University's Nature Preserve
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk. Free parking in non-paid lots like Lot M on weekends.

cards.title: Browse the Art Museum
cards.subtitle: Global art in the Fine Arts Building
cards.notes: View a permanent collection of over 4,500 objects and rotating exhibitions. Admission is always free for students and the general public.
cards.short_summary: A public campus museum hosting diverse exhibitions and a significant permanent collection of global artworks.
cards.evidence_claim: The Binghamton University Art Museum offers a dynamic schedule of exhibitions that are free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Visit the Art Museum - Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Saturday, 12:00 PM – 4:00 PM, with extended hours until 7:00 PM on Thursdays.

cards.title: Free Late Night Bowling
cards.subtitle: Bowling in the Union Undergrounds
cards.notes: Roll strikes with friends at the campus bowling alley. Undergraduate and graduate students bowl for free; shoe rentals are just 50 cents.
cards.short_summary: A student-focused bowling alley offering free lane access for currently enrolled Binghamton students.
cards.evidence_claim: Bowling is free for currently enrolled undergraduate and graduate students at The Lanes in the Union Undergrounds.
cards.source_title: Activities | The Union | Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Open until midnight on Fridays and Saturdays. Student ID required for free access.

cards.entity_name: E.W. Heier Teaching and Research Greenhouse
cards.title: Visit the Exotic Greenhouse
cards.subtitle: Four biomes in the Science Complex
cards.notes: Walk through tropical, desert, and temperate environments housing over 6,000 plants. It is a warm, free escape during cold Binghamton winters.
cards.short_summary: A large campus greenhouse facility featuring four distinct climate zones and a massive collection of exotic plant species.
cards.evidence_claim: The greenhouse is open to the public Monday through Friday from 9:00 AM to 3:30 PM with no admission fee mentioned.
cards.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions | Greenhouse - Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Open Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM – 3:30 PM. Best for small groups of 10 or fewer.

cards.title: Relax on the Peace Quad
cards.subtitle: The central hub for campus events
cards.notes: Lounge on the grass or attend major free events like University Fest. It is the primary outdoor social space between the Union and Fine Arts.
cards.short_summary: A central campus green space used for student gatherings, outdoor studying, and large-scale university festivals.
cards.evidence_claim: The Peace Quad hosts major free events like University Fest and the Party on the Peace Quad for the campus community.
cards.source_title: University Fest | Campus Activities
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible 24/7; major events typically occur during the academic year.

cards.title: Workout at FitSpace
cards.subtitle: Free cardio and strength training
cards.notes: Access cardio equipment and the functional training zone for free. Just bring your Binghamton University ID card to enter the facility.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus fitness center offering free access to exercise equipment for all current students.
cards.evidence_claim: Students get FREE access to the FitSpace fitness center by showing their BingU ID card.
cards.source_title: FitSpace Free Access - B-Engaged
cards.access_notes: Located in the East Gym. Requires a valid student ID for entry.

cards.title: Study in the Memorial Courtyard
cards.subtitle: Quiet retreat in the Fine Arts Building
cards.notes: Find a bench under the willow tree in this enclosed courtyard. It is a peaceful, free spot for reading or de-stressing between classes.
cards.short_summary: A secluded outdoor courtyard located within the Fine Arts Building, known for its tranquil atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: The Memorial Courtyard is a hidden gem in the center of the Fine Arts Building, featuring benches and flowerbeds for relaxation.
cards.source_title: 13 Hidden Gems On Binghamton University's Campus
cards.access_notes: Accessible during Fine Arts Building operating hours, typically 7:00 AM – 11:00 PM.

cards.title: Watch a Free Movie
cards.subtitle: Weekly films in the Undergrounds
cards.notes: Catch popular pre-release films on Friday nights in the Union. Snacks are often provided, and admission is free for all current students.
cards.short_summary: A weekly film screening series for students featuring recent movies and free snacks in the University Union.
cards.evidence_claim: Late Nite Cinema is a weekly series featuring popular films on Friday nights, free for all current Binghamton University students.
cards.source_title: Late Nite | Campus Activities - Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Friday nights during the academic year. Located in the Undergrounds Lounge.

cards.title: Attend a Skills Lab
cards.subtitle: Professional workshops for all majors
cards.notes: Join 90-minute hands-on workshops led by industry professionals. Learn skills like data analytics or project management at no cost.
cards.short_summary: Free professional development workshops hosted by the career center to help students gain industry-relevant skills.
cards.evidence_claim: The Fleishman Center's Skills Lab program provides free workshops for students to learn industry-relevant skills.
cards.source_title: Skills Labs | Fleishman Career Center - Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Workshops are held throughout the semester; registration via hireBING is usually required.

cards.title: Play Open Gym Sports
cards.subtitle: Basketball, pickleball, and swimming
cards.notes: Drop in for open swim or court sports like basketball and pickleball. Equipment like balls and racquets can be checked out for free with an ID.
cards.short_summary: Free access to gym courts and the pool for recreational use, including complimentary sports equipment loans.
cards.evidence_claim: The East Gym offers free recreational activities, including open swim, pickleball and basketball, with a student ID.
cards.source_title: 10 Campus Hacks to Help Make the Most of Your Time at Binghamton!
cards.access_notes: Check the B-Engaged app for weekly open recreation and pool schedules.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: From stomping on winter coats to high-fiving a bronze bearcat, Binghamton University's traditions reflect a unique blend of Upstate resilience and residential community spirit.

cards.title: Stepping on the Coat
cards.subtitle: A Defiant Farewell to Winter
cards.notes: Join the annual spring ritual of stomping on a winter coat to ward off late-season snow. This tradition dates back to 1966 and is now a highlight of the Spring Fling festival.
cards.short_summary: A symbolic ceremony where students stomp on a winter coat to demand the arrival of spring weather.
cards.evidence_claim: The tradition began in April 1966 when student Larry Kressel stomped on his coat in defiance of a late snowfall; it is now held annually during Spring Fling.
cards.source_title: 'Stepping on the Coat' heralds spring - Binghamton News
cards.access_notes: Open to all students during the annual Spring Fling event on the Peace Quad or Spine.

cards.title: Co-Rec Football
cards.subtitle: The Battle for Residential Bragging Rights
cards.notes: Compete in this long-standing 6-on-6 flag football league where residence halls face off. Founded in Hinman College in 1971, it remains a cornerstone of campus social life.
cards.short_summary: A highly competitive inter-dormitory flag football league that has defined residential life since the 1970s.
cards.evidence_claim: Co-Rec football was founded in Hinman College in 1971 and involves teams from every residential community competing for a championship.
cards.source_title: Hinman College Traditions | Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Games are held on the Co-Rec fields near the residential communities during the fall semester.

cards.title: Casino-in-the-Woods
cards.subtitle: Legal Gambling for a Good Cause
cards.notes: Visit the College-in-the-Woods dining hall for the one night a year it transforms into a licensed casino. All proceeds from the games benefit local charities.
cards.short_summary: An annual charity event where a dining hall becomes a fully licensed casino featuring student dealers.
cards.evidence_claim: Casino-in-the-Woods is one of the oldest traditions at CIW, operating as a state-licensed casino for one night to raise money for charity.
cards.source_title: College-in-the-Woods Traditions | Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Held annually in the CIW Dining Hall; a small entrance fee is typically required for charity.

cards.title: High-Fiving the Bearcat
cards.subtitle: A Ritual for Good Luck
cards.notes: Stop by the bronze bearcat statue on the Spine to high-five its paw. Students perform this ritual for good luck on exams or as a greeting during campus tours.
cards.short_summary: A superstition involving high-fiving the bronze mascot statue to ensure academic success.
cards.evidence_claim: New students walk down the Spine and high-five 'Bingturong,' the bearcat statue, for good luck as part of B-Welcome traditions.
cards.source_title: 5 Can't-Miss Events to Start the Semester - Binghamton News
cards.access_notes: The statue is located outdoors on the Spine near the University Union and is accessible 24/7.

cards.title: Tower Glow
cards.subtitle: Lighting the Way for the New Year
cards.notes: Gather on the Spine the night before classes begin to watch the Glenn G. Bartle Library Tower light up in Binghamton green. The event features music and street food.
cards.short_summary: A ceremonial lighting of the campus's most iconic landmark to mark the start of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: Tower Glow is a tradition where the Library Tower is lit green the night before classes begin, accompanied by games and food.
cards.source_title: 5 Can't-Miss Events to Start the Semester - Binghamton News
cards.access_notes: Visible from the Spine and Peace Quad; the event takes place annually in late August.

cards.title: The Class of B Photo
cards.subtitle: A Human Letter Formation
cards.notes: Join your entire incoming class to form a massive human 'B' for a commemorative photo. This tradition marks your official entry into the Bearcat community.
cards.short_summary: An annual event where the freshman class assembles to form the university's 'B' logo for an aerial photograph.
cards.evidence_claim: New students parade to the East Gym to take the annual Class of B Photo as part of the New Student Kickoff.
cards.source_title: 5 Can't-Miss Events to Start the Semester - Binghamton News
cards.access_notes: Held at the East Gym or nearby fields during Welcome Weekend for new students.

cards.title: Salamander Days
cards.subtitle: Celebrating the Nature Preserve Migration
cards.notes: Celebrate the spring migration of spotted salamanders in the campus Nature Preserve. Mountainview residents host themed events to honor these local amphibians.
cards.short_summary: A community-specific tradition celebrating the annual salamander crossing in the university's nature preserve.
cards.evidence_claim: Salamander Days is a popular tradition in the Mountainview Community where students celebrate the crossing of salamanders in the Nature Preserve.
cards.source_title: Campus Traditions and Events - Binghamton News
cards.access_notes: Events are centered around the Mountainview residential community and the adjacent Nature Preserve.

cards.title: Passing the Vegetable
cards.subtitle: An Appeal for a Mild Winter
cards.notes: Look for this quirky fall ritual where students pass vegetables to appeal to Mother Nature for a mild winter. It's a legacy tradition from the SUNY Binghamton era.
cards.short_summary: A historical fall tradition involving the communal passing of vegetables to influence the upcoming winter weather.
cards.evidence_claim: The tradition was started in 1975 by student Richard Agriss to appeal to Mother Nature for a mild winter.
cards.source_title: You Know You Went to SUNY Binghamton When… - Binghamton News
cards.access_notes: Primarily a legacy tradition, occasionally revived by alumni or student groups in the fall.

cards.title: Late Nite Binghamton
cards.subtitle: Weekend Entertainment Underground
cards.notes: Head to the Union Undergrounds on Friday and Saturday nights for free movies, bowling, and themed activities. It's the campus standard for alcohol-free weekend fun.
cards.short_summary: A long-running program providing late-night weekend entertainment and social activities for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Late Nite Saturdays host large-scale events including escape rooms, casino nights, and carnivals in the University Union.
cards.source_title: Late Nite | Campus Activities - Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Events typically run from 8 PM to 1 AM on Friday and Saturday nights during the semester.

cards.title: Restaurant Week Pilgrimage
cards.subtitle: A Semesterly Culinary Tradition
cards.notes: Join the mass student migration to Downtown Binghamton for fixed-price multi-course meals. It's a biannual tradition that connects the campus with the local food scene.
cards.short_summary: A biannual event where students frequent local downtown restaurants for discounted three-course meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Binghamton Restaurant Week is a recurring event in fall and spring where students and residents enjoy deals at local iconic spots like Lost Dog Café.
cards.source_title: Restaurant Week Fall 2025 - Pipe Dream
cards.access_notes: Participating restaurants are located throughout Downtown Binghamton; accessible via OCCT buses.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at Binghamton University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: Build a plausible under-21-safe first-weekend sequence, not a ranking. Give each card one role in the sequence and use evergreen places or recurring behaviors rather than one-time events. Be conservative about hours, access, and travel time unless directly sourced.

cards.title: Kick Off with Friday Bowling
cards.subtitle: University Union West
cards.notes: Start your weekend at the Undergrounds. Bowling is free for students; just bring 50 cents for shoe rentals. It's a central hub for meeting new people in a relaxed setting.
cards.short_summary: A student-focused recreation center featuring free bowling, billiards, and table tennis.
cards.evidence_claim: Bowling is free for currently enrolled undergraduate and graduate students with a 50 cent shoe rental fee.
cards.source_title: Activities | The Union | Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Open Friday until 12:00 a.m. and Saturday from 2:00 p.m. to 12:00 a.m.

cards.title: Join the Late Nite Crowd
cards.subtitle: University Union
cards.notes: Head to the Union on Friday or Saturday nights for free movies, casino nights, or carnivals. It is the primary weekend alternative to off-campus nightlife.
cards.short_summary: An award-winning weekend programming series offering free entertainment and prizes for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Late Nite Binghamton provides students with a variety of activities on Friday and Saturday evenings, including free movies and large-scale events.
cards.source_title: Late Nite | Campus Activities - Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Events typically run Friday and Saturday nights from 8 p.m. to midnight.

cards.title: Saturday Morning Hike
cards.subtitle: Nature Preserve
cards.notes: Walk the Pond Trail to the iconic wooden bridge. It's a flat, easy path perfect for a quiet morning outdoors before the day's events pick up.
cards.short_summary: A 190-acre on-campus preserve featuring wetlands, a six-acre pond, and maintained hiking trails.
cards.evidence_claim: The Pond Trail starts behind College-in-the-Woods and leads to a famous bridge overlooking Harpur Pond.
cards.source_title: 5 Gorgeous Nature Preserve Trails You Must Hike This Fall - Binghamton News
cards.access_notes: Open daily from dawn to dusk; accessible from multiple campus parking lots.

cards.title: Lunch at the MarketPlace
cards.subtitle: University Union
cards.notes: Grab lunch at local favorites like Chick-N-Bap or Royal Indian. It's the social heart of campus dining and accepts meal plan dining dollars.
cards.short_summary: A central dining food court in the University Union featuring diverse retail food concepts.
cards.evidence_claim: The MarketPlace features regional favorites like Chick-N-Bap and is a hub for student dining.
cards.source_title: Dining Services | Auxiliary Services - Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Hours vary by vendor; typically open for lunch and dinner on weekdays with limited weekend hours.

cards.title: Cheer at the Events Center
cards.subtitle: Bearcats Sports Complex
cards.notes: Join the boisterous student section for a Bearcats game. It's the largest sports facility in the region and the best place to show school spirit.
cards.short_summary: A 5,142-seat multi-purpose arena that serves as the home for Binghamton Bearcats basketball.
cards.evidence_claim: The Events Center includes a student section that seats more than 1,000 members of the BU community.
cards.source_title: Events Center - Facilities - Binghamton University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Accessible during scheduled athletic events and university ceremonies.

cards.title: Find Your Study Spot
cards.subtitle: Library Tower
cards.notes: Explore the North or East Reading Rooms for quiet study. Finding your preferred corner early helps you stay ahead once classes begin on Monday.
cards.short_summary: The university's main library, housing collections in humanities, social sciences, and fine arts.
cards.evidence_claim: Designated quiet study spaces include the East Reading Room (1st floor) and North Reading Room (2nd floor).
cards.source_title: Group Study Rooms and Study Spaces | Libraries - Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Open daily during the academic year; check website for specific floor hours.

cards.title: Navigate via OCCT
cards.subtitle: Campus-Wide
cards.notes: Learn the bus routes by taking a loop on the student-run OCCT. It's free with your ID and connects the campus to downtown Binghamton and local shops.
cards.short_summary: A student-run transit service providing transportation around the university and local community.
cards.evidence_claim: OCCT provides transportation around the Binghamton University community at no cost with a scan of a valid student ID.
cards.source_title: Buses and Shuttles | Transportation and Parking Services - Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Regular service runs daily; Late Nite shuttles operate Friday and Saturday nights.

cards.entity_name: Recreation Center at the East Gym
cards.title: Sunday Afternoon Open Rec
cards.subtitle: East Gym
cards.notes: Visit the East Gym for open recreation. You can play basketball, pickleball, or go for a swim just by signing in with your student ID.
cards.short_summary: The primary campus fitness and recreation facility offering gym courts, a pool, and fitness equipment.
cards.evidence_claim: All currently enrolled students have access to the Recreation Center at the East Gym for drop-in activities like basketball and swimming.
cards.source_title: Campus Recreation | Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Open Saturday 9 a.m. - 8 p.m. and Sunday with regular academic year hours.

cards.entity_name: Anderson Center for the Performing Arts
cards.title: Catch a Show at Watters Theater
cards.subtitle: Fine Arts Building
cards.notes: Check the schedule for a student production or visiting artist. It's a great way to experience the campus arts scene before the semester gets busy.
cards.short_summary: A premier performing arts complex featuring the Osterhout Concert Theater and Watters Theater.
cards.evidence_claim: The Anderson Center features multiple performance spaces including the Osterhout Concert Theater and Watters Theater.
cards.source_title: Anderson Center for the Performing Arts - Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Open for scheduled performances and workshops; ticket prices vary by event.

cards.title: Photo with Baxter the Bearcat
cards.subtitle: University Union West
cards.notes: Find the statue of Baxter the Bearcat on the second floor of the Union. It's a classic spot for a first-weekend photo to commemorate your start at Bing.
cards.short_summary: A popular photo spot featuring a life-sized statue of the university mascot, Baxter.
cards.evidence_claim: Baxter's lookalike is located on the second floor of University Union West, right outside the Bookstore.
cards.source_title: The Union | Binghamton University
cards.access_notes: Accessible during University Union building hours.
